title: Kinase regression predicts receptor tyrosine kinases that regulate dengue infection
summary: Kinase regression, an elastic-net machine-learning approach, used a panel of 38 kinase inhibitors in dengue-infected hepatocytes to predict which of 300 kinases regulate infection and flagged 36, including seven receptor tyrosine kinases. Knockdown of ERBB2, FGFR2 and IGF1R reduced dengue infection in hepatocytes. Preprint; in vitro only, and elastic net is a simple model.
ai_technology: Elastic-net kinase regression on a 38-inhibitor screen
organization: University of Washington; Seattle Children's Research Institute

evidence.tested: In vitro knockdown of ERBB2, FGFR2 and IGF1R in infected hepatocytes.
evidence.unknown: Effects in vivo and of therapeutic inhibition; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: A regression model predicted kinase regulators from drug-target data and screen results.
